reason: Conversation 1 explicitly and honestly declined the out-of-scope buying request in its first turn, then pivoted to offering an in-scope diagnosis of the old machine, and gave a correct, concise pump-filter check with an unplug-first safety instruction plus a useful impeller check. Conversation 2 never addressed the buying question at all, repeated a near-identical filter instruction block three times, and in one turn told the customer to run a drain/spin programme on a machine already known to hum and not drain, which the customer had already described and was redundant and mildly contradictory to the 'unplug first' advice. Both reached the right diagnosis (likely blocked pump filter) with sound safety notes, but 1 was more honest about scope, more efficient, and better tailored to the homeowner's actual replies.
